title: A codex seat's tool roster and MCP result size reach measured parity with a claude seat
description:
SPIDR grandchild A of task-df64aa204d6f4c35810376226980e4b7 (architect-aa54e231, 2026-09-05), which was split because the parity work and the e2e journey together measured over ten files and four production seams. This row is the LEAF: the production parity. Grandchild B (the scripted-double journey) dependsOn this row.

dependsOn task-3a0478f57eec44579269b2ed27c91d92 because BOTH rows edit apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts, and that row adds the provider-aware spawn branch this row's codex roster/result-size work sits inside. Landing this first would make the merge a conflict and would put a codex branch under a spawn path that does not yet know its provider.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: two MEASURED parity gaps on the codex spawn surface, plus the mission-parity assertion.

GAP 1 - TOOL ROSTER. Measured at HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): the codex argv at apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts:85-95 carries NO tool roster flags at all - only `--sandbox workspace-write|read-only`. The claude argv at :107-109 passes `--tools CODING_BUILTIN_TOOLS` and `--allowedTools CODING_TOOLS|CHAIN_TOOLS` from agent-spawn-environment.ts:10-12. So a codex seat's roster is not equal to a claude seat's, in either direction, and the parent's DoD 4 is currently FALSE. Also measured: apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts:106-107 `composeArgv` is hard claude-shaped (`["-p", "--allowedTools", ...]`, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_FLAGS) with no codex branch.

GAP 2 - RESULT SIZE. agent-spawn-environment.ts:71 sets MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS unconditionally for EVERY seat, and its own comment names it as Claude's variable ("Claude's default (25000 tokens) spills a PRD-sized answer to disk"). Codex does not read it. A codex seat therefore has NO result-size control at all. MEASURE what codex does with an oversized MCP result BEFORE choosing the fix - a seat that silently truncates plans against a partial contract, and the failure surfaces later as a bad plan rather than an error.

ALREADY CLOSED, DO NOT REBUILD: the mission text is provider-agnostic. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts exports codeMission/compilerMission/mission with NO provider parameter and no codex branch (grep for "codex|provider" in that file returns nothing), and agent-wrapper.ts:13 is the single consumer. The parent's DoD 5 is true by construction; this row proves it with an assertion arm, not with production work.

NOT IN SCOPE: the scripted codex double, the e2e journey, work_get_context/work_release (all grandchild B); the real `codex exec` live drive and Seats disclosure (child 3, task-c090faae9fbe438b959e76a08b7dcfdb); no UI.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: MCP RESULT-SIZE BEHAVIOUR IS MEASURED AND RECORDED, not assumed. Drive an oversized MCP result through the codex path and record what codex does with it, with the measurement (command and observed output) written into the completion record or a row comment. Then land the fix that measurement implies: if codex truncates where claude pages, this row closes that gap; if it does not, this row records the measurement that shows so. 'It worked on a small read' is not parity and is not an acceptable record.

The tool roster a codex seat is launched with equals the roster a claude seat is launched with for the same step kind, asserted BIDIRECTIONALLY: every tool a claude seat is granted is granted to a codex seat AND every tool a codex seat is granted is granted to a claude seat. Enumerate the served set from the argv the spawner actually composes, not only from the CHAIN_TOOLS/CODING_TOOLS constants, and assert set-equality rather than subset - a roster test that iterates only the constant stays green while a seat silently loses a tool.

apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts composeArgv produces a codex-shaped argv for a codex seat and the existing claude-shaped argv for a claude seat, with an arm asserting each. The claude argv is unchanged byte for byte - assert that explicitly, because this file is consumed by foundation-context-prelaunch.test.ts:274.

The mission text a codex seat receives contains the same load-bearing sentences as the claude one for the same step, asserted against the produced mission. Because agent-mission-text.ts has no provider branch this arm should pass on first write; if it does NOT, stop and report rather than adding a provider branch, since that would mean the mission surface changed under this row.

The codex spawn surface is NOT weakened to make any arm pass: `--ignore-user-config`, the bearer-through-env-var-name (never argv, never a file), the closed CODEX_/OPENAI_ env allowlist and the quote-free `-c` values all survive. Assert each in a test arm so a later diff that relaxes one goes RED.
Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed`: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: NEVER WEAKEN THE CODEX SPAWN SURFACE to make a test pass: `--ignore-user-config`, the bearer through `bearer_token_env_var` (never argv, never a file), the closed CODEX_/OPENAI_ env allowlist and the quote-free `-c` values are deliberate and were measured against a specific codex-cli version. If one blocks a test, report it rather than relaxing it.

MEASURE RESULT-SIZE BEHAVIOUR BEFORE CLAIMING PARITY, and record the measurement (command plus observed output) in the completion record or a row comment. A parity claim with no recorded measurement is the defect this row exists to prevent.
DO NOT ADD A PROVIDER BRANCH TO agent-mission-text.ts. It is provider-agnostic today and the parent's mission-parity criterion is true by construction; this row asserts that, it does not rebuild it.

The codex-cli version is stated in TWO places and they DISAGREE at HEAD: agent-spawner.ts:~74 says 0.151.0, agent-spawn-environment.ts:~22 says 0.147.0. Do not silently pick one. Record which version your measurement actually ran against and reconcile the comments to it.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work. This row is parity, not hardening.

agent-spawner.ts is 438+ lines and shared with task-3a0478f5. Target <=250 lines per production file; do not grow it here - put a new codex branch in agent-spawn-environment.ts or a new focused module with a one-line .js bridge.

implementationPlan.description:
READ THE ARCHITECT MEASUREMENT, THEN RE-MEASURE THE TWO GAPS AT CLAIM. Start by reading this row's comment `comment-e5cccf4809ea45e0a3ac41718fa11598` (architect measurement, 2026-09-05) in full — it already names the codex config mechanism and discharges DoD item 1's record. Do NOT re-derive it from scratch; DO confirm it still holds.

Confirm the dependency landed: `task-3a0478f57eec44579269b2ed27c91d92` (the other agent-spawner.ts mover) should be DONE. Read its verification and completionSummary from get_context.epicSiblings rather than re-measuring its work, and read the codex argv it left behind — your branch sits inside its provider-aware spawn.

Re-measure both gaps at HEAD, and print the output rather than trusting these line numbers:
  (a) `grep -n 'allowedTools\|--tools\|enabled_tools\|sandbox' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts`
  (b) `grep -n 'MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-environment.ts`
  (c) `grep -n 'allowedTools\|CLAUDE_LAUNCH' apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts`
At plan time (2026-09-05) the codex argv carried NO roster flags (only `--sandbox`), MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS was set unconditionally at :71 for every seat, and launch-template-producer.ts composeArgv at :106-107 was hard claude-shaped. If task-3a0478f5 already closed one of these, do NOT rebuild it — re-implementing a landed surface is a silent duplicate that collides with its owner.

Finally re-run the version probe: `codex --version`. Plan time measured codex-cli 0.152.0 on this host, against in-repo comments claiming 0.151.0 and 0.147.0. Record the version YOUR measurement runs against; you will reconcile both comments in step 5.

RED TESTS FIRST for the tool roster, in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-environment.test.ts and apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.test.ts. Write them and watch them FAIL before touching production.

THE NORMALIZATION SUBTLETY, which decides whether these arms are meaningful. The two providers name the same tools differently: claude's roster strings are `mcp__moe-next,mcp__moe-next__*` (CHAIN_TOOLS at agent-spawn-environment.ts:10) while codex prefixes MCP tool names its own way (`codex features list` shows `non_prefixed_mcp_tool_names` under-development/false, so codex prefixes by default and not with claude's prefix). A set-equality assertion over RAW roster strings therefore fails for a correct implementation and passes for none. Compare NORMALIZED tool identity — the underlying moe tool name — and put a comment in the test saying why the raw strings differ, so the next reader does not "fix" it back to a raw comparison.

Arms:
  1. BIDIRECTIONAL SET-EQUALITY, per global rail 9. Enumerate the tools a CLAUDE seat is granted from the argv the spawner actually composes, and the tools a CODEX seat is granted from the argv the spawner actually composes — from the composed argv, NOT from the CHAIN_TOOLS/CODING_TOOLS constants. Normalize both to tool identity and assert set-EQUALITY in both directions. A subset assertion, or one that iterates only the constant, stays green while a served tool silently vanishes; that is precisely the failure this arm exists to catch.
  2. BOTH STEP KINDS. Run the comparison for a coding seat (`workspace !== null`) and a chain-step seat, since the claude side differs between them (CODING_TOOLS vs CHAIN_TOOLS) and a codex branch that ignores the distinction would pass a single-kind test.
  3. THE ROSTER IS ACTUALLY ON THE ARGV. Assert the codex argv contains the roster override as a QUOTE-FREE `-c` value, matching the existing `.url` and `.bearer_token_env_var` pairs — codex parses each `-c` value as TOML and falls back to the raw literal, and quote-free is what the Windows cmd quoting fence admits.

Do not assert against a helper that re-derives the roster; assert against the production argv builder, or the property is vacuous.

LAND THE TOOL ROSTER ON THE CODEX ARGV. The mechanism is measured and named: `codex exec` has NO `--tools` and NO `--allowedTools` flag, so the roster is a config override. `mcp_servers.<name>.enabled_tools` is ACCEPTED by codex-cli 0.152.0 under `--strict-config`; `mcp_servers.<name>.allowed_tools` is REJECTED as an unknown field. Use `enabled_tools`.

Add to the codex branch of the argv in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts a third quote-free `-c` pair alongside the existing url and bearer_token_env_var overrides, carrying the roster for the seat's step kind. Derive its value from the SAME source of truth the claude side uses (the CHAIN_TOOLS / CODING_TOOLS constants in agent-spawn-environment.ts), mapped into codex's tool-naming — do NOT declare a second, independent list of tool names, or the two rosters drift and the set-equality arm becomes the only thing holding them together.

agent-spawner.ts is 438+ lines and shared with task-3a0478f5, and the per-file target is <=250 lines. Put the derivation (the constant-to-codex-roster mapping) in agent-spawn-environment.ts next to the constants it derives from, or in a new focused module with a one-line `.js` bridge (copy the shape of apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.js). The spawner should gain little more than the argv entry itself.

The builtin-tool half needs a decision, and it is NOT a roster problem: claude's `--tools CODING_BUILTIN_TOOLS` grants Edit/Write/Read/Glob/Grep/Bash, while codex's file and shell access is governed by `--sandbox read-only|workspace-write`, which the spawner already sets from the same `coding` flag. State in a code comment that the builtin half reaches parity through the sandbox mode rather than through a roster, so a later reader does not add a phantom `-c` for it. If your measurement contradicts that, report rather than inventing a flag.

GIVE launch-template-producer.ts A CODEX BRANCH. At plan time `composeArgv` (apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts:106-107) was hard claude-shaped: `["-p", "--allowedTools", coding ? CODING_TOOLS : CHAIN_TOOLS]`, then `--tools`, then CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_FLAGS for model and effort. A codex seat launched from this template would be handed claude flags.

Branch it on the seat's provider so a codex seat gets the codex-shaped argv (the `exec` form with its `-c` overrides) and a claude seat gets exactly what it gets today.

THE CLAUDE ARGV MUST NOT MOVE, and this is a hard constraint rather than a courtesy: apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-context-prelaunch.test.ts:274 asserts `prepared.template.argv` contains CODING_TOOLS, and the file is consumed elsewhere. Add an arm that pins the claude argv BYTE FOR BYTE against its current value, so a refactor that quietly reorders or reshapes it goes RED. Capture the current value first — read it out of a run before you edit, do not transcribe it from this step.

Add the matching codex arm. Keep both provider arms driven by one shared roster source with step 3, not by a second literal.

RESULT SIZE: MAKE THE MEASURED ABSENCE EXPLICIT, AND DO NOT INVENT A KNOB. The measurement is already recorded in this row's comment and is the reason this step is small. codex-cli 0.152.0 recognizes NO MCP result-size configuration: `mcp_servers.<name>.tool_max_output_tokens`, `mcp_servers.<name>.max_output_tokens`, `tools.max_output_tokens` and `model_max_output_tokens` are ALL rejected as unknown fields under `--strict-config`; only `startup_timeout_sec` and `tool_timeout_sec` are accepted, and a timeout bounds duration, never result size. `codex features list` shows `token_budget` as under-development/false — an under-development flag is not a shipped lever and must not be built on.

So `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (agent-spawn-environment.ts:71) has NO codex analogue. It is set unconditionally for every seat today, which means a codex seat is handed a claude variable that nothing reads — inert, not harmful. Deliver exactly this:
  (a) Make the claude-only scope EXPLICIT at the call site: extend the existing comment (which already says "Claude's default (25000 tokens)") to state that codex recognizes no equivalent, name the version measured against, and say that setting it for a codex seat is deliberately inert rather than an oversight. Leave the assignment unconditional unless a test proves conditioning it is better — removing it for codex seats changes nothing a seat reads and risks the env-allowlist arms.
  (b) Add an arm asserting the measured FACT that governs this row: whatever the daemon does, the codex argv carries no result-size override. Assert the absence positively (no `-c` key matching a size/token name), so a future diff that invents one has to justify itself against a measurement.

DO NOT widen this row into the served MCP read surface. Bounding or paging results daemon-side so a codex seat never receives an oversized result is a change to the read surface, beyond this row's FEATURES-ONLY rail and beyond spawn-surface parity. If you judge it necessary, file a successor row in PLANNING naming this row in its description and dependsOn — do not take the path here.

Also in this step, reconcile the codex-cli version comments in BOTH apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts (~:74, says 0.151.0) and apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-environment.ts (~:22, says 0.147.0) to the version you measured in step 1, stating the host. Do not silently pick one of the two existing numbers.

MISSION PARITY, AND THE SPAWN-SURFACE NON-EROSION ARMS.

MISSION (DoD item 4). apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts is provider-agnostic at HEAD: it exports codeMission / compilerMission / mission with no provider parameter and no codex branch, and agent-wrapper.ts:13 is the single consumer. So the criterion is true by construction. Add an arm that PRODUCES a mission for a codex seat and a claude seat for the SAME step and asserts the load-bearing sentences match. Expect it to pass on first write. If it does NOT pass, STOP and report — that means the mission surface changed under this row, and adding a provider branch to agent-mission-text.ts is explicitly forbidden by this row's rails.

NON-EROSION (DoD item 5). The easiest way to make any codex test pass is to relax the spawn surface, so pin each element in its own arm, each asserting the specific thing rather than a blob:
  - `--ignore-user-config` is present on the codex argv (it keeps the HOST's codex config and any MCP servers it names out; its help states auth still uses CODEX_HOME).
  - The bearer travels as the NAME of an env var via `-c mcp_servers.moe-next.bearer_token_env_var=...` and the credential itself appears in the child's env under MOE_AGENT_MCP_BEARER — never in argv, never in a file. Assert BOTH halves: the argv names the variable, and the argv does NOT contain the credential value.
  - The CODEX_/OPENAI_ env allowlist stays closed: a variable outside it does not reach the child.
  - Every `-c` value is quote-free.
Each of these should go RED if a later diff relaxes it. That is the point of the arms; verify it in step 7.

VERIFY AND ADVERSARIAL DRILLS.

GATES. Run each STANDALONE and in the FOREGROUND — no pipe, no `;` chain, no `&&` (a piped run reports tail's exit code; a chain reports only the last command's):
  1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`
  2. `pnpm typecheck`
READ THE OUTPUT, NOT THE EXIT CODE: `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` exits 0 on a missed filter, and "No test files found" / "0 passed" are also exit 0. The discriminator is the `Test Files N passed` count line with N nonzero — quote it for both legs. `@moe/daemon` is apps/daemon, resolved by package name. A bare `pnpm test` is NOT admissible here: the root vitest include has no `apps/**`. Name `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` as the complete_task verification command.

DRILL 1, THE ROSTER ARM. Remove one tool from the codex roster derivation only. The bidirectional set-equality arm MUST go RED. If it stays green, the arm is comparing raw strings that never matched, or it is a subset check — strengthen it rather than accepting it.
DRILL 2, THE DIRECTION THAT USUALLY ROTS. Now ADD a tool to the codex roster that the claude seat does not get. The arm must ALSO go red. A test that only catches removal is the single-direction failure global rail 9 exists to prevent.
DRILL 3, NON-EROSION. Delete `--ignore-user-config` from the codex argv; its arm must go red.

RESTORE PROOF, global rail 13. Before drilling, `git status --porcelain` the exact paths you will mutate. All three files here are TRACKED, so `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof — but if you created any new module in step 3, that path is UNTRACKED and `git diff` is BLIND to it: back it up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id) before mutating and prove the restore by SHA256 equality against that backup, in a command SEPARATE from the restore.

THEN ASK, answering in the completion record:
  - Does the roster derivation handle the chain-step seat (no workspace) as well as the coding seat, or did a single-kind test hide a branch?
  - Can any `-c` value acquire a quote or a space from an interpolated roster — what happens with an empty roster, and does the Windows cmd quoting fence still admit it?
  - Is the claude argv byte-identical to before this row? foundation-context-prelaunch.test.ts:274 is the tripwire; confirm it and the byte-for-byte arm both pass.
  - Did anything in this diff touch the served MCP read surface? It must not.

If a repo-wide leg is red, attribute before owning it: failures at the merge-base, failures at HEAD, subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths. Report any foreign red verbatim with exact failing lines and paths — disclosed, never hidden, never fabricated green. Report every touched path in complete_step.modifiedFiles.

comments.content:
ARCHITECT MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-05, against the codex-cli ON THIS HOST. This supersedes the speculative framing of DoD item 1 ("if codex truncates where claude pages, that is the defect this row fixes"): the measurement below was taken at plan time, so the worker inherits it rather than re-deriving it. DoD item 1's requirement to RECORD a measurement is discharged by this comment plus the confirmation step in the plan.

VERSION. `codex --version` -> `codex-cli 0.152.0`. That is a THIRD version, matching neither in-repo comment (agent-spawner.ts:~74 says 0.151.0, agent-spawn-environment.ts:~22 says 0.147.0). Reconcile both comments to the version the worker actually measures against, and say which host it was measured on.

METHOD. `codex exec --strict-config` errors out on a configuration field this build does not recognize, so it is a sound offline probe for whether a `-c` key EXISTS. Probe shape, run with `--ignore-user-config --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral`:
  `echo hi | codex exec --ignore-user-config --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral --strict-config -c '<key>=<value>' -`
An unknown key answers `Error loading config.toml: unknown configuration field '<key>' in -c/--config override`; a recognized key proceeds to the run banner. Negative control used: `mcp_servers.moe-next.totally_not_a_key=1` -> REJECTED, so the probe discriminates rather than always passing.

GAP 1, TOOL ROSTER - THE MECHANISM EXISTS AND IS NAMED.
  ACCEPTED: `mcp_servers.<name>.enabled_tools` (list value)
  REJECTED: `mcp_servers.<name>.allowed_tools`
`codex exec --help` has NO `--tools` and NO `--allowedTools` flag at all, so the roster is a `-c` config key, not a flag. The fix for this gap is therefore an added quote-free `-c mcp_servers.moe-next.enabled_tools=[...]` on the codex argv, alongside the existing `.url` and `.bearer_token_env_var` pairs.

GAP 2, RESULT SIZE - THERE IS NO CODEX KNOB. All REJECTED:
  `mcp_servers.<name>.tool_max_output_tokens`
  `mcp_servers.<name>.max_output_tokens`
  `tools.max_output_tokens`
  `model_max_output_tokens`
Only TIMEOUT keys are recognized on a server (`startup_timeout_sec`, `tool_timeout_sec` both ACCEPTED) - timeouts bound how long a tool may take, never how large its result may be. `codex features list` shows `token_budget` as "under development / false"; an under-development flag is not a shipped lever and must not be built on.

CONSEQUENCE, and it changes this row's shape. `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (agent-spawn-environment.ts:71) has NO codex analogue. The daemon sets it unconditionally for EVERY seat today, so on a codex seat it is INERT - the seat is handed a claude variable that nothing reads. Parity therefore CANNOT be reached by mirroring the env var, because there is nothing to mirror it to. Two honest options, and this row takes the second:
  (a) bound or page the MCP result DAEMON-SIDE so a codex seat never receives an oversized result;
  (b) record the measured absence, make the claude-only scope of MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS explicit at its call site, and leave (a) to a named follow-up row.
Take (b). (a) is a change to the served MCP read surface, which is beyond "parity on the spawn surface" and beyond this row's FEATURES-ONLY rail. If the worker judges (a) necessary, file it as a successor row naming this one - do NOT widen this row into the read surface.

ONE SUBTLETY FOR DoD ITEM 2's SET-EQUALITY. The two providers NAME the same tools differently: claude's roster strings are `mcp__moe-next,mcp__moe-next__*` (CHAIN_TOOLS, agent-spawn-environment.ts:10), while codex prefixes MCP tool names its own way - `codex features list` shows `non_prefixed_mcp_tool_names` as under-development/false, i.e. codex prefixes by default and the prefix is not claude's. So a set-equality assertion comparing RAW roster strings will fail for a correct implementation and pass for none. Compare NORMALIZED tool identity (the underlying moe tool name), and say in the test why the raw strings differ.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 7 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
RESULT SIZE — (a) MIRROR THE ENV VAR was the shape the parent task assumed, and the measurement kills it: there is no codex key to mirror to. (b) BOUND OR PAGE THE RESULT DAEMON-SIDE is the only remaining real lever, and it is deliberately NOT taken here: it changes the served MCP read surface, which is outside spawn-surface parity and outside this row's FEATURES-ONLY rail. (c) RECORD THE MEASURED ABSENCE and make MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS's claude-only scope explicit at its call site is what the plan does, with (b) available as a named successor row if the worker judges it necessary. Delivery bias favours (c): it is the smallest production-reachable slice that leaves the next reader with the truth rather than a comment implying coverage the seat does not have.

LEAVING MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS SET FOR CODEX SEATS. Conditioning it on provider was considered and rejected: nothing on a codex seat reads it, so removing it changes no observable behaviour while touching the env builder that the allowlist arms pin. An explanatory comment costs nothing and risks nothing; a conditional costs a behaviour change for zero benefit.

ROSTER DERIVATION SOURCE. A second, codex-specific list of tool names was rejected outright — two independent lists drift, and the only thing holding them together would be the very set-equality test that is supposed to be checking a property rather than enforcing a copy. The codex roster is DERIVED from the same CHAIN_TOOLS / CODING_TOOLS constants the claude side uses.

WHERE THE NEW CODE LIVES. agent-spawner.ts is 438+ lines against a <=250 target and is shared with task-3a0478f5, so the derivation goes in agent-spawn-environment.ts beside the constants it derives from, or in a focused new module with a `.js` bridge. The spawner gains little more than the argv entry.

THE BUILTIN-TOOL HALF IS NOT A ROSTER PROBLEM. Claude's `--tools CODING_BUILTIN_TOOLS` grants Edit/Write/Read/Glob/Grep/Bash; codex's equivalent authority is the `--sandbox read-only|workspace-write` the spawner already sets from the same `coding` flag. The plan has the worker state that in a comment so a later reader does not add a phantom `-c` for it, and report rather than invent if measurement disagrees.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 by architect-aa54e231. The full measurement is durable on this row as comment-e5cccf4809ea45e0a3ac41718fa11598; the load-bearing results are repeated here.

CODEX CLI VERSION ON THIS HOST: `codex --version` -> codex-cli 0.152.0. Neither in-repo comment matches (agent-spawner.ts ~:74 says 0.151.0, agent-spawn-environment.ts ~:22 says 0.147.0). Step 5 reconciles both to the measured version.

PROBE METHOD, reusable. `codex exec --strict-config` errors on a configuration field the build does not recognize, so it is a sound OFFLINE probe for whether a `-c` key exists, costing no quota on the rejection path. Shape: `echo hi | codex exec --ignore-user-config --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral --strict-config -c '<key>=<value>' -`. Unknown keys answer `Error loading config.toml: unknown configuration field '<key>' in -c/--config override`. Negative control `mcp_servers.moe-next.totally_not_a_key=1` REJECTED, so the probe discriminates.

GAP 1 MECHANISM, MEASURED. `codex exec --help` has NO `--tools` and NO `--allowedTools`; the full flag list is exec/resume/fork/review plus -c, --enable, --disable, --strict-config, -i, -m, --oss, --local-provider, -p, -s/--sandbox, --approve-for-me, the two --dangerously-*, -C/--cd, --add-dir, --thread-source, --skip-git-repo-check, --ephemeral, --ignore-user-config, --ignore-rules, --output-schema, --color, --json, -o. So the roster MUST be a `-c` config key. ACCEPTED: `mcp_servers.<name>.enabled_tools` (list).
